- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for early days of the 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly (5–15%) for first 5–7 days of horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >1.5x recent mean), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated overshoot; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply downward correction starting from day 10–15 of forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon: if forecast is >2.0 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 0.1–0.3 per day until convergence to recent mean.
- For sentiment history with high volatility (alternating 0.67 and -0.33), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average before output.
